title: Canonical normalized comparisons for strict-tower realization
statement: For an adic coefficient datum $d$ on $(A,I)$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], construct the following comparisons for pro-etale module sheaves. The completed and constant strict tower operations are those of [def-weil-pbc-strict-tower-operations] and [def-cbc-strict-constant-tower-operations]; open extension and its coefficient/quotient comparisons are fixed by [def-cbc-strict-tower-open-extension] and [def-cbc-completed-open-scalar-quotient-interface]. For schemes $T,S$, coefficient ring sheaves $R_T,R_S$, and an additive exact functor $F:\operatorname{Mod}(R_T)\to\operatorname{Mod}(R_S)$, write $F^{\mathrm{Tow}}$ for postcomposition on strict towers and $L_T,L_S$ for derived inverse limits [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit]. The constant-tower/derived-limit adjunction determines the comparison $F^D L_T\to L_S(F^{\mathrm{Tow}})^D$ as the mate of the identity constant-diagram square. When $F$ preserves countable products this mate is invertible [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit]. Apply it to scalar restriction and quasi-compact open extension to obtain the specified scalar/limit and open/limit isomorphisms. Direct image/limit is the conjugate of the constant/pullback square, including both adjunction units [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits]; scalar/direct-image is the derived normalized coefficient comparison [lem-weil-pbc-strict-tower-exchange-mate-normalization]. Using these maps, form the source and target presentations of the proper/open composite for compactifications [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], and their open-factor endpoints for a Cartesian open square [def-cbc-open-immersion-square]. The source first applies the completed-pullback projection, scalar/limit, proper corner and quotient/open comparisons; the target applies inverse direct-image/limit, inverse open/limit, inverse completed-pullback, inverse scalar/open and inverse scalar/direct-image comparisons, in that order. These are actual constructions, with no freely chosen endpoint isomorphism. Their naturality and finite evaluation are the component naturality and evaluation formulas of these same maps. This node records the comparison constructions and already proved auxiliary properties extracted from the realization module; it asserts neither the completed compact-support realization identity nor its completed open-factor identity.
